item.title: Spirit’s Old Data Redraws Mars’s Watery Past
item.summary: Rover data from more than 20 years ago has revealed clues to the existence of liquid water on ancient [Mars](https://spectrum.ieee.org/tag/mars). [NASA’s Spirit rover](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mer-spirit/) carried a specialized instrument called a [Mössbauer spectrometer](https://an.rsl.wustl.edu/help/Content/About%20the%20mission/MER/Instruments/Moessbauer%20Spectrometer.htm) that performed mineralogical analyses of soil, rock, and dust on the surface of the red planet at [Gusev Crater](https://science.nasa.gov/resource/gusev-crater/). Individual measurements didn’t always indicate definitive proof of water, but when scientist [Paolo de Souza](https://www.ecu.edu.au/about-ecu/executive-team/professor-paulo-de-souza) of Edith Cowan University in Australia examined years’ worth of measurements together, a definite pattern began to show up in the existence of minerals that could only exist in the presence of water. His analysis shows that Mars used to sport a lot more water than scientists expected. De Souza was particularly interested in the existence of hematite and altered magnetite measured in the Martian soil. These two minerals often form when rocks interact with water.
